sentence: This project tests whether long-read sequencing can find drug-resistant bacteria and bacteriophages at low cost during local infection outbreaks.
This project builds a small portable tool that detects trace amounts of psychoactive substances such as fentanyl and xylazine.
This project provides support and open communication among investigators working on translational research for brain cancer.
This project supports collaboration that speeds up the development of devices made for children.
This project builds imaging tools to capture how electrical impulses travel through the living, beating heart of an early avian embryo in 3D.
This project studies how obesity changes normal metabolic pathways in ways that lead to cancer risk in humans.
This project uses a technique called Electron Spin Resonance to study how viruses attack cells and how proteins interact with membranes.
This project explores the mechanisms that help form the brain circuits that process sounds during development.
This project examines how social determinants of health and epigenomic factors relate to psychological symptoms in women receiving breast cancer treatment.
This project brings data science into high school chemistry and biology classes through drug discovery.
This project studies how tumors keep T-cells out and how tumor molecules weaken T-cells, to find treatments for patients who resist immunotherapies.
This project studies how the structure of native murine polyomavirus particles varies in mouse epithelial cell lines.
This project studies how Kaposi's sarcoma arises from oral mesenchymal stem cells that respond to hypoxia.
This project uses genetic data and brain samples to find out how mutant blood cell clones protect against Alzheimer's disease.
This project tests a combination treatment for succinate dehydrogenase deficient gastrointestinal stromal tumors and creates a biobank of these tumors.
This project uses proteomics and functional genomics to find what controls mu-opioid receptor activation.
This project uses deep learning to design chimeric proteins that recognize bacteria and recruit host immune receptors to destroy antibiotic-resistant strains.
This project studies how a protein found only in glutamatergic synapses of interneurons helps organize the postsynaptic density.
This project uses brain imaging to look for markers that describe Chiari malformation and predict how patients respond to surgery.
This project tracks how the birth of neurons from stem cells changes with aging and Alzheimer's disease.
